subject: Media Literacy
title: The Inverted Pyramid
description: A quick, practical guide to The Inverted Pyramid.

hook.text: Newspaper stories put the most important facts first. If you only read the headline, you get the gist.

buildup.text: The inverted pyramid structure starts with who, what, when, where, and why — then adds detail.

discovery.text: This format was invented during the Civil War when telegraph lines could cut off mid-message.

twist.text: Online news flipped this — clickbait headlines hide the key fact to force you to click through.

climax.text: The structure of a story tells you whether it's designed to inform or to generate clicks.

punchline.text: Good journalism answers questions. Clickbait withholds them.

quiz.question: Why was the inverted pyramid structure invented?
options: Telegraph lines could cut off mid-message during the Civil War
